Subject: Post-demo: data handling & residency questions

Hi Ava / Peter —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Short recap and a couple of asks to make sure we capture your data-handling requirements correctly before we move to legal / infra checks: 

Summary of requirements we noted on the call:
- Training-on-customer-data: your team flagged that you may want to opt out of any usage of customer data for model training or model improvement.
- PII handling: customer-sensitive fields must be redacted/hashed at ingest; no raw PII persisted for training.
- Logging & retention: session logs should be retained for troubleshooting but limited to a 90-day rolling window unless otherwise required for audit.
- Audit logs: security/audit logs (access, config changes) retained for 12 months.
- Data residency: all production inference and logs to remain in us-east-1 (US only).
- Encryption & KMS: keys managed by DataCorp KMS integration preferred (bring-your-own-key).

Ask: can you confirm (in writing) whether DataCorp is formally requesting an opt-out from any use of your data for model training or model improvement? If yes, we will: 1) add an explicit opt-out clause to the DPA and SOW, 2) open an engineering ticket to ensure training pipelines are excluded, and 3) set logging/retention controls per above.

Attachments: I can share a working DPA with the opt-out clause and our security-questionnaire responses for your team to review.

Next steps (proposed):
- Peter: confirm opt-out in writing (one-line reply is fine)
- Marissa (me) & Legal: update DPA and send revised doc
- Rishi (cc): assess feasibility and timeline for implementing retention/residency controls (we typically can scope a patch within 2 weeks for dedicated customers)

Thanks — want to make this as low-friction as possible.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling & residency questions

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This email serves as written confirmation of DataCorp's data handling decisions following today's discovery: 

1) Training opt-out: DataCorp formally opts out of Redwood using any customer-provided data (including inputs, system messages, and derived embeddings) for model training or model improvement. This opt-out applies to both online and offline training pipelines.

2) PII: We require that any fields identified as PII are either redacted or hashed on ingest; Redwood must not persist raw PII for any training purpose.

3) Retention: Application-level logs (chat history, request/response payloads) retained for a maximum rolling 90 days for troubleshooting. Security & audit logs retained for 12 months.

4) Residency & encryption: All inference and logs must remain in the US (us-east-1). We will require customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for encryption at rest.

5) Evidence & attestation: Please provide the updated DPA that includes the explicit opt-out language, plus answers to the security questionnaire (SOC 2 controls mapping, encryption details, access controls).

We also have a short procurement checklist — can you send the signed DPA and a stub of the DocuSign link once ready?

Thanks,
Peter Liu
Security & Privacy Lead, DataCorp
peter.liu@datacorp.com
